p: Group outings can be tricky. Some people love a bit of competition, others are a bit nervous. Karting works brilliantly for both, as long as you plan it right.

If you've got a mixed group, have a word with staff when booking about the best session format. Splitting into heats can stop the nervous drivers feeling overwhelmed, while the speed demons still get to battle it out.
Agree a few ground rules too. Keep it clean on track, give each other room and leave the aggressive moves at home. Staff take safety seriously, and a race full of shunts isn't fun for anyone.
Make the results part of the fun. A daft prize for last place, or the winner buying the first round, keeps the banter flowing long after the race is over.
Book ahead for weekends, when the slots fill fast.

Sheffield's city centre has plenty of places to celebrate afterwards. The Millennium Gallery, next to the Winter Garden, is free and showcases the city's metalwork heritage alongside changing exhibitions. The Peace Gardens, with their fountains, are the city's favourite meeting spot on a sunny day. And Sheffield's independent food and drink scene, especially around Kelham Island and Division Street, means you'll never be short of somewhere to toast the winner. With the Peak District right on the doorstep, a group hike the next day is a great way to round off a weekend.
